subject: fix: create the temporary PuTTY private-key file atomically
body:
fix: create the temporary PuTTY private-key file atomically

Address review feedback on PR #3260.

- PuttyBase: the temp private-key file (extracted from a credential
  vault) was created with GetRandomFileName() + File.WriteAllText(),
  which is non-atomic and could overwrite a pre-existing file. Replaced
  with a WriteTemporaryPrivateKeyFile helper that opens the file with
  FileMode.CreateNew (never overwrites), retries on a name collision,
  and sets the Temporary attribute. The cleanup in finally only ever
  targets a path this helper successfully created.
- Build_mR-NB.yml: grant `contents: write` to the Create-Combined-Release
  job — it uses softprops/action-gh-release to create the tag/release
  and upload assets, which needs that permission (per Kvarkas's review).

Build clean; full suite 2003/83, matching the baseline (the changed
PuttyBase.Connect path has no unit-test coverage).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

security_flags.reason: CI workflow changes are the primary supply-chain vector (pull_request_target abuse, workflow injection)

triage.rationale: Target reopens an already-created key path; reimplement exclusive creation while preserving secure wipe. Omit superseded CI permissions; this still does not close PuTTY handoff race.

votes.concern: Helper can leak partially written private keys when write or attribute failures occur, because retry logic bypasses caller cleanup.
votes.reason: Current code already atomically reserves temp files and securely wipes them; the CI permission already exists, making this stale patch duplicative and regressive.

votes.concern: Unrelated CI permissions churn; atomic temp-key write is marginal and not import-clean.
votes.reason: Idea fits credential safety, but mixed commit and tiny gain—reimplement only if still missing.
